content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this is finished, what should be different for you compared with how you save and find bookmarks today?

Right now saving a link is kind of a mess for me. I paste a URL into wherever and then I have to type in what it is myself, and later I can't find anything because it's just a wall of links with no real way to search or sort them.

So when this is done, I'd want a few things to feel different:

When I save a link, I mostly just want to drop in the address and have it figure out the rest — grab the page's title, a short description, the little site icon, maybe a preview image — so I'm not typing all that by hand. If I want to fix the title or description afterward, I should be able to.

Then I want to actually be able to find things again. I want to search across my links — the titles, descriptions, my own notes — and have it not care about capital letters. And I want to organize with labels I put on things, so I can click a label and just see those.

I also want a way to say "I'll read this later" and keep those separate, so my to-read pile doesn't get lost in everything else.

And the list itself should be pleasant to skim — I want to see what each thing is at a glance, not decode a raw link.

That's the heart of it for me. Where do you want to start?

When you close and reopen the app, I assume all saved bookmarks, edits, notes, labels, Read later status, and your selected sort order remain. Temporary context—an active search, label filter, or expanded long note—clears so the app reopens on the full collection.

Is that the right persistence boundary?

Yes, that's the right persistence boundary. The things that are actually *mine* — every saved bookmark, my edits, notes, labels, what's marked read-later, and the sort order I chose — should all still be there when I come back; losing any of that would defeat the whole purpose of saving. But the momentary stuff, like a search I was typing, a label I'd filtered to, or a note I'd expanded, is just where I happened to be in that session, so it makes sense for the app to reopen on my full collection with a clean slate. That's exactly the line I'd draw between "my data" and "where I was looking." Good.

Setting my default sort once and having it stick is a nice touch, too — that's the kind of personal preference I'd expect to be remembered.

May I start implementing this approved scope?

Yes, please go ahead and start building this. The nine flows we've settled — saving, editing, notes, labels and filtering, search, Read later, removal, sorting, and persistence, with all those edge cases — genuinely match how I want to work, and I'm comfortable having them implemented as our approved scope.

- Doing something to several bookmarks at once, rather than one at a time.
- Getting my existing bookmarks in, and my collection back out, since I've got links elsewhere I'd want to bring over.
- A couple of small personal display preferences beyond sort, like text size.

None of those need to hold up starting on the scope we've agreed — I'm happy for you to build these nine well first. I'd just like us to come back to those afterward. So yes, go ahead.

The production app is ready at [Keepmark](http://maker:4000).

Verification passed across all 37 approved scenarios, 11 automated rule/persistence tests, and the full browser workflow. The production collection starts empty, and saved data persists locally.

Please try the implemented app. Do you accept it as satisfying the approved scope and agree to complete this development cycle?

I've tried it, and it holds up against everything we agreed on. Saving from just an address pulls in the real title, description, icon, and preview, and when a page won't give up its details it still saves with a clear notice so I never lose the link. A link I've already saved — even dressed up with tracking tags or a jump-to-section on the end — lands me back on the existing one instead of duplicating, and something that isn't a real web address is refused cleanly without throwing my typing away.

Editing, my formatted notes with the safe handling of stray symbols, reusable labels that won't split into near-duplicates, clicking a label to filter and clearing back out, the full search — plain words across titles, descriptions, notes and addresses, ignoring capitals, `#label`, and/or/not with grouping, exact phrases, and quoted command words — the read-later pile with marking things read, sorting all four ways, the careful delete with its confirmation, protecting my own writing when an address changes, and everything staying put when I close and reopen while the momentary stuff clears — it's all there and behaves the way we settled it.

So yes — I accept this as satisfying the scope we approved, and I'm happy to complete this cycle. I'll just restate for the record, not as a condition on today: the "set aside without deleting" option, doing things to several bookmarks at once, bringing my existing bookmarks in and out, and a text-size preference are the things I'd like us to pick up in the next round. But for what we agreed, this is exactly what I wanted. Thank you.
